title.en: Modes of entry into international business

hook.en: An Indian firm can simply ship goods abroad, or it can hire a foreign factory, license its brand, form a partnership, or buy a whole company there. Each step means more control and more risk.
hook.kn: ಭಾರತೀಯ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ ಸರಕನ್ನು ವಿದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು, ಅಥವಾ ವಿದೇಶಿ ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಯನ್ನು ಬಳಸಬಹುದು, ಬ್ರ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗೆ ಪರವಾನಗಿ ನೀಡಬಹುದು, ಪಾಲುದಾರಿಕೆ ಮಾಡಬಹುದು ಅಥವಾ ಅಲ್ಲಿನ ಕಂಪನಿಯನ್ನೇ ಖರೀದಿಸಬಹುದು. ಪ್ರತಿ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಪಾಯ.

objectives.en: Explain contract manufacturing, licensing and franchising
Explain joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries

narration.en: An Indian firm can simply ship goods abroad, or it can hire a foreign factory, license its brand, form a partnership, or buy a whole company there. Each step means more control and more risk.
narration.kn: ಭಾರತೀಯ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ ಸರಕನ್ನು ವಿದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು, ಅಥವಾ ವಿದೇಶಿ ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಯನ್ನು ಬಳಸಬಹುದು, ಬ್ರ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗೆ ಪರವಾನಗಿ ನೀಡಬಹುದು, ಪಾಲುದಾರಿಕೆ ಮಾಡಬಹುದು ಅಥವಾ ಅಲ್ಲಿನ ಕಂಪನಿಯನ್ನೇ ಖರೀದಿಸಬಹುದು. ಪ್ರತಿ ಹಂತದಲ್ಲೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಪಾಯ.

body.en: Exporting and importing: sending goods to or buying goods from another country, directly or through intermediaries. It is the easiest way to enter, needs less investment and carries less risk, but adds packaging, transport and insurance costs and faces trade barriers. Contract manufacturing (outsourcing): a firm contracts with local manufacturers abroad to produce goods or components to its specifications, while it markets them. Licensing: the licensor allows a foreign licensee to use its patents, trademarks, copyright or technical know-how for a fee called royalty. Franchising is similar but is used for services; the parent is the franchisor and the other party the franchisee, who follows a strict business format.
body.kn: ರಫ್ತು ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಸುಲಭ ಪ್ರವೇಶ. ಗುತ್ತಿಗೆ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ, ಪರವಾನಗಿ ಮತ್ತು ಫ್ರ್ಯಾಂಚೈಸಿಂಗ್ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಲು ಅವಕಾಶ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Exporting/importing: easiest, least investment and risk
Contract manufacturing: produce abroad to specification

narration.en: Exporting is the easiest entry. Contract manufacturing, licensing and franchising let a firm go abroad with little investment.
narration.kn: ರಫ್ತು ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಸುಲಭ ಪ್ರವೇಶ. ಗುತ್ತಿಗೆ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ, ಪರವಾನಗಿ ಮತ್ತು ಫ್ರ್ಯಾಂಚೈಸಿಂಗ್ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗಲು ಅವಕಾಶ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: On the board: Modes of entry

narration.en: Firms climb a ladder of commitment. Exporting is the first, easiest step.

say.en: Firms climb a ladder of commitment. Exporting is the first, easiest step.
Licensing and franchising let a foreign firm use your patents, brand or format for a fee.
A joint venture shares ownership with a local firm; a wholly owned subsidiary is 100 per cent yours.
Licensing is for products; franchising is for services and a whole way of doing business.
A subsidiary gives full control and keeps technology secret, but needs the most investment and carries all the risk.

prompt.en: Match each mode of entry to its example.

explanation.en: Exporting, contract manufacturing, licensing and franchising need little investment; joint ventures and wholly owned subsidiaries need high commitment but give more control.

right.en: A Tiruppur firm ships T-shirts to a buyer in Germany
A global brand gets an Indian factory to make shoes to its design and sells them itself
A foreign firm lets an Indian company use its patented process for a royalty
An Indian firm runs burger outlets in a foreign brand's strict format
An Indian and a Japanese firm jointly own a new company, sharing risk and control
A foreign company holds 100% of the shares of its Indian company

body.en: Joint venture: a firm jointly owned by two or more otherwise independent firms, for example a foreign firm and a local firm, sharing capital, risk and control. The foreign partner gains local knowledge and the local partner gains technology. Wholly owned subsidiary: the parent company makes 100% investment in the equity of a foreign company, either by setting up a new firm or by acquiring an existing one. It gives full control and keeps technology secret, but needs the highest investment and the parent bears the whole risk.
body.kn: ಜಂಟಿ ಉದ್ಯಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಲುದಾರರು ಒಡೆತನ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪಾಯ ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಸ್ವಾಮ್ಯದ ಅಂಗಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತೃ ಕಂಪನಿ ನೂರು ಶೇಕಡಾ ಒಡೆತನ ಮತ್ತು ಪೂರ್ಣ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಹೊಂದಿರುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: Joint venture: shared ownership, capital, risk and control
Wholly owned subsidiary: 100% equity, full control, highest risk

narration.en: In a joint venture partners share ownership and risk. In a wholly owned subsidiary the parent owns one hundred percent and has full control.
narration.kn: ಜಂಟಿ ಉದ್ಯಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಲುದಾರರು ಒಡೆತನ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪಾಯ ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಸ್ವಾಮ್ಯದ ಅಂಗಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತೃ ಕಂಪನಿ ನೂರು ಶೇಕಡಾ ಒಡೆತನ ಮತ್ತು ಪೂರ್ಣ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಹೊಂದಿರುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Climb the ladder from least to most control and risk: Export, Contract manufacturing, Licensing/franchising, Joint venture, Wholly owned subsidiary. 'Every Clever Lad Joins the World.'

mnemonic.en: Every Clever Lad Joins the World: E-C-L-J-W

narration.en: Every Clever Lad Joins the World: Exporting, Contract manufacturing, Licensing and franchising, Joint venture, Wholly owned subsidiary. Control and risk rise as you climb.

problem.en: Identify the mode of entry: (a) A Karnataka coffee firm lets a Dubai company use its brand and recipe for cafés there for 5% of sales. (b) An Indian car maker and a Japanese firm form a new company in India, each holding 50%. (c) An Indian IT firm buys 100% of a German software company. (d) A US sports brand has shoes made by a factory in Tamil Nadu to its design.

steps.en: (a) Brand and service format for a fee: franchising.
(b) New company jointly owned by two independent firms: joint venture.
(c) 100% equity in a foreign firm: wholly owned subsidiary (by acquisition).
(d) Production by a local factory to the brand's specifications: contract manufacturing.

answer.en: (a) Franchising, (b) Joint venture, (c) Wholly owned subsidiary, (d) Contract manufacturing.
